content.text:
The core answer: the Default Persona is one shared, read-only Egma persona. It is not copied for each customer. Its system prompt combines: 1. A fixed Egma instruction. 2. The Default Persona’s traits. 3. The current test’s scenario. 4. The full conversation history. This is exact for current `origin/main`, commit `e68cb90ce2f03bef95561718917d183e39e0aaa9`. I did not inspect the hosted deployment, so this does not prove which commit its containers run. ## The complete flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A["One shared Default Persona v1"] --> B["New project points to it"] B --> C{"Does the test name personas?"} C -- "No" --> D["Test version saves the project's default persona ID"] C -- "Yes" --> E["Test version saves the selected persona IDs"] D --> F["Run pins the current persona version"] E --> F F --> G["Claim API builds SimulationSpec v3:
traits + models + test scenario + current provider keys"] G --> H["Simulator builds the system prompt"] H --> I{"Has the customer agent spoken?"} I -- "Yes" --> J["Add agent words as role: user"] I -- "No" --> K["Add hidden opening nudge as role: user"] J --> L["OpenAI gpt-4o-mini
system prompt + full history"] K --> L L --> M["Persona reply"] M --> N{"Contains [CONCLUDED]?"} N -- "No" --> O{"Chat or voice?"} O -- "Chat" --> P["Send text to the customer agent"] O -- "Voice" --> Q["Cartesia turns text into audio"] P --> R["Customer agent answers"] Q --> S["OpenAI STT turns agent audio into text"] R --> T["Append both turns to history"] S --> T T --> L N -- "Yes" --> U["Remove marker and end"] U --> V["Store turns and timing spans"] V --> W["Finish simulation and create grading work"] ``` I refreshed Graphify for this checkout: 1,069 code files, 11,284 nodes, and 28,876 post-cluster edges. Its queries centered on `projectDefaultPersona`, `resolvePersonaVersions`, `assembledSpec`, `RunningSimulation`, `Persona`, and `messages_for`. The API-to-simulator step crosses a JSON contract, so I checked both ends directly in the source. [Open the fresh Graphify call-flow export](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/visualizations/2026/08/25/01a03642-a2bb-74d3-9510-3c7ae83c3f8c/egma-persona/egma-persona-callflow.html) ## The exact system prompt Only the marked test scenario changes: ```text You are playing a person in a live conversation with a customer service agent. You are the person; the agent is who you are talking to. Who you are, exactly as authored: { "accent": "Neutral American English.", "backgroundNoise": "None.", "language": "en-US", "manner": "Clear, natural, and conversational.", "patience": "Starts patient and gives the agent time to explain.", "personality": "Speaks clear, natural English. Starts patient and cooperative, answers one question at a time, and becomes firmer if the agent is confusing or repetitive without becoming rude.", "underFriction": "Becomes firmer if the agent is confusing or repetitive, without becoming rude." } Why you are here today: How to conduct yourself: - Stay in character as this person for the whole exchange. Never mention being simulated, tested, or an AI. - Speak one conversational turn at a time, in plain spoken words — no lists, no headings, no stage directions. - Pursue what you came for until it is concluded to your satisfaction, and let your persona decide how patiently. - When your goal is concluded and nothing further is needed, say a brief goodbye and end your reply with [CONCLUDED]. ``` The exact template and role mapping are in [persona.py](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/persona.py:24). The exact Default Persona traits are in [catalog.ts](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/db/src/persona-library/catalog.ts:54). There is no single universal final prompt because every test supplies a different scenario. ## What is sent to the LLM If the customer agent has not spoken, the first request has this shape: ```json { "model": "gpt-4o-mini", "messages": [ { "role": "system", "content": "" }, { "role": "user", "content": "(The conversation is open and the agent is listening. Speak your first turn.)" } ] } ``` If the customer agent greets first, its greeting replaces that hidden nudge. On later calls: - Customer-agent turns use `role: "user"`. - Persona turns use `role: "assistant"`. - Egma sends the complete accumulated history each time. - The hidden opening nudge is not stored as a transcript turn. Egma sends `POST https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions`. The body contains only `model` and `messages`. Egma does not set temperature, token limits, tools, seed, `top_p`, or penalties. The timeout is 60 seconds. See [model.py](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/model.py:179). ## Exact models for Default Persona v1 | Function | Exact selection | |---|---| | Persona LLM | OpenAI `gpt-4o-mini` | | Voice transcription | OpenAI `gpt-live-transcribe` | | Text-to-speech | Cartesia `sonic-3.5` | | Cartesia voice ID | `5ee9feff-1265-424a-9d7f-8e4d431a12c7` | | Speaking speed | `1` | | Voice activity detection | Silero in shipped Docker Compose; this is deployment configuration, not persona content | The repository has no human-readable name for that Cartesia voice ID. Chat simulations use only the LLM. Voice simulations use the same LLM plus OpenAI realtime transcription and Cartesia speech. The selections come from the immutable persona version; there is no simulator model or voice fallback. See [model catalog](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/packages/db/src/models/catalog.ts:24) and [speech.py](/Users/nischalj10/.codex/worktrees/8669/egma/apps/simulator/src/egma_simulator/speech.py:413). Provider keys are separate from the persona. For each simulation, the API loads the current OpenAI and Cartesia keys from AWS Secrets Manager in Egma Cloud, or from environment variables in self-hosted Egma. You are an agent in a team of agents collaborating to complete a task.

You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents. All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.

When you provide a response in the final channel, that content is immediately delivered back to your parent agent.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```
Message Type: NEW_TASK | MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
You may also see them addressed as to=/root/..., which indicates your identity is /root/...

Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. Only set `model` or `reasoning_effort` when explicitly requested by the user, applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions, or skill instructions; when doing so, set `fork_turns` to `"none"` or a positive integer string.

Use sub-agents when parallel work would materially improve speed or quality. This mode remains active until a later multi-agent mode developer message changes it.</multi_agent_mode>

# egma

The first open-source platform purpose-built to help teams shipping voice agents gain trust in the agent they ship to production.

**If `egma-planning/AGENTS.md` exists in your checkout, read it now and follow it in full** — it carries additional instructions for this repo. If it doesn't exist, ignore this and carry on; nothing here depends on it.

# communication rules

0. ALWAYS use the built in /wait-what skill while communicating to the developer.
1. whenever you are taking to the developer iterating on this project with you - speak in simple human language, no overcomplicated jargons. always talk in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. 
2. trace the full story (what is being worked on, why its important, what's the decsion in front and its consequences). be truthful. 
3. for a batch of UI annotations, inventory every comment first, group the work by product surface with one owner per surface, finish each group before one independent review, then run one integrated test, build, and browser proof.

# design system

Before any visual or interaction change, read `DESIGN.md` in full. It is the product design source of truth. Do not change its locked palette, styling architecture, or the Egma logo without explicit developer approval. Treat its type, component shape, dark mode, and motion rules as current product rules. In UI review, flag code that does not follow `DESIGN.md`.
# egma — internal agent instructions

This private repository is the planning half of the public Egma code repository. Read this file whenever it is present.

## Repository roots

- **Planning root:** the Git repository containing this file. From the Egma code root, its path is `egma-planning/`.
- **Code root:** the parent Egma Git repository when this checkout is nested in its standard internal location.

All internal plans, tickets, research, domain terms, architecture decisions, and specifications live in the Planning root. Source code, tests, builds, and public documentation live in the Code root.

These are separate Git repositories. Commit planning changes in the Planning root and code changes in the Code root. A request to commit changes can require one commit in each repository.

## Agent skills

### Planning root

Repository configuration overrides the default planning paths in installed Matt skills.

Resolve these paths from the Planning root:

- `CONTEXT.md`
- `docs/adr/`
- `docs/agents/`
- `.scratch/`
- `.out-of-scope/`

Resolve every other repository path from the Code root unless the task says otherwise. Skill-local paths, such as a template beside a `SKILL.md`, remain relative to that skill.

### Issue tracker

Use the local Markdown tracker under `.scratch/<effort>/`. See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.

The Planning root is private and separately version-controlled. All internal documentation stays here. This positional rule removes the need to decide which parts of a planning document are safe to publish.

### Triage labels

Use the five canonical triage roles and write their values to the issue file's `Status:` line. See `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`.

### Domain docs

This project uses one domain context. Use `CONTEXT.md` as the glossary and `docs/adr/` for architecture decisions. See `docs/agents/domain.md`.

The settled vocabulary is `test` → `test suite` → `run` → `simulation`, with `grader` for judgment logic, `persona` for the synthetic caller, and `agent` only for the customer's agent under test. `eval` names nothing.

## Matt skill maintenance

When the developer invokes `/update-matt-skills`, read and follow `.agents/skills/update-matt-skills/SKILL.md`. The skill updates the public copies, restores their generic path-routing block, and verifies every tracked Matt skill.

## Pull-request reviews

Greptile reviews every public pull request automatically and can comment in several waves. Keep fixes in the same branch. Answer a review thread when its recommendation is not applied. A pull request is ready to hand off when every Greptile thread is fixed or answered.

## Keep the public repository quiet

The public `AGENTS.md` carries one conditional pointer to this file. Other public files must stand on their own and must not explain the private planning repository. Write public documentation for external readers instead of copying internal material.

SSM command ID: bbc4e71a-e423-4685-bcba-e8b0b9b47f5c
{
    "Status": "Success",
    "ResponseCode": 0,
    "Output": "DEPLOY_SCRIPT
#!/bin/bash
# Replace what the platform box is running with a named build.
#
#   /opt/egma/deployment/deploy.sh <ref>
#
# The deploy workflow in the public repository invokes this over SSM, after
# syncing this whole directory fresh from S3. It is equally a script to run by
# hand on the box when nobody wants to drive a deployment through CI.
#
# ## The layout, and the rule behind it
#
#   /opt/egma/deployment/   this directory. Synced from S3 with --delete on
#                           every deploy, so nothing in it can drift — it IS
#                           the egma-cloud repository's deployment/ folder
#   /opt/egma/egma/         egma's own repository, checked out at the ref
#                           being deployed. Rebuilt whenever it is missing
#   /opt/egma/certs/        the Supabase root, fetched when missing
#   /opt/egma/.env          assembled fresh on every deploy, root-only
#
# Nothing under /opt/egma is authored on the box. Every file either arrives
# from a repository (via S3 or git) or is derived at deploy time. That rule is
# the fix for 2026-08-15, when hand-written files on this box drifted behind a
# rename in the code and took the persona's settings down silently.
set -euo pipefail

REF="${1:-latest}"
REGION="${AWS_REGION:-${AWS_DEFAULT_REGION:-us-east-1}}"
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
WORK="$(cd "$HERE/.." && pwd)"
CODE="$WORK/egma"

# ── egma's own files, at the commit the images were built from ───────────────
# The compose files and the images must come from one commit. Deploying an
# image built from one tree with compose files from another is how a setting
# goes missing without anything failing.
if [ -d "$CODE/.git" ]; then
  git -C "$CODE" fetch --tags --quiet origin
else
  git clone --quiet https://github.com/egma-ai/egma.git "$CODE"
fi
if git -C "$CODE" rev-parse --verify --quiet "$REF^{commit}" >/dev/null; then
  git -C "$CODE" checkout --quiet --detach "$REF"
  echo "egma files at $REF ($(git -C "$CODE" rev-parse --short HEAD))"
else
  git -C "$CODE" checkout --quiet --detach origin/main
  echo "no ref '$REF' in the repository; using origin/main for the compose files"
fi

# ── The Supabase root ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Fetched rather than committed: it is a published file, and its address is in
# the egma/db/supabase secret under ca_url. Without it the API dies at boot
# reporting a self-signed chain.
if [ ! -s "$WORK/certs/supabase-ca.crt" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$WORK/certs"
  curl -fsSL \
    "$(aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id egma/db/supabase \
        --region "$REGION" --query SecretString --output text \
      | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["ca_url"])')" \
    -o "$WORK/certs/supabase-ca.crt"
  echo "fetched the Supabase root certificate"
fi

# ── The settings ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Assembled fresh every time, so changing a secret and deploying is enough.
# assemble-env.sh refuses to write anything if settings.map does not answer
# every setting egma's compose files ask for — a gap stops the deployment here
# rather than reaching production.
bash "$HERE/assemble-env.sh" "$WORK/.env" "$CODE"

ACCOUNT="$(aws sts get-caller-identity --query Account --output text)"
REGISTRY="${EGMA_REGISTRY:-${ACCOUNT}.dkr.ecr.${REGION}.amazonaws.com}"

# The registry and tag join the assembled settings rather than being exported,
# so a `docker compose` run by hand afterwards sees exactly what the deployment
# saw rather than resolving to something else.
printf 'EGMA_REGISTRY=%s\nEGMA_IMAGE_TAG=%s\n' "$REGISTRY" "$REF" >> "$WORK/.env"

# One flag controls every platform telemetry path. The api and grader read it
# themselves. The collector is a Compose profile, so this deployment maps the
# same value to that profile. Anything but `on`, including an absent value,
# also removes a collector left running by an earlier enabled deployment.
PLATFORM_TELEMETRY="$(awk -F= '
  $1 == "EGMA_TELEMETRY" {
    value = substr($0, index($0, "=") + 1)
    gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", value)
    print tolower(value)
    exit
  }
' "$WORK/.env")"

COMPOSE_PROFILE_ARGS=()
if [ "$PLATFORM_TELEMETRY" = "on" ]; then
  COMPOSE_PROFILE_ARGS=(--profile platform-telemetry)
fi

# --project-directory anchors every relative path in the stack — ./certs, the
# env_file — to /opt/egma, whichever file names it.
compose() {
  docker compose \
    -f "$CODE/docker-compose.yml" \
    -f "$CODE/docker-compose.managed.yml" \
    -f "$HERE/local.yml" \
    --project-directory "$WORK" \
    --project-name egma "${COMPOSE_PROFILE_ARGS[@]}" "$@"
}

# Activate the collector profile only for this cleanup command. Stop and
# remove it before the rest of the deploy when the flag is off. A failed
# removal stops the deploy; it must not say telemetry is off while an old
# collector still sends data.
if [ "$PLATFORM_TELEMETRY" != "on" ]; then
  compose --profile platform-telemetry rm --stop --force otel-collector
  echo "platform telemetry: off"
fi

aws ecr get-login-password --region "$REGION" \
  | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin "$REGISTRY"

# `--no-build` matters: egma's compose file builds all three services from
# source, which is right for a self-hoster and wrong here. CI built these
# already, and this box holds a read-only pull credential on purpose.
compose pull
compose up -d --wait --wait-timeout 300 --no-build
compose ps
if [ "$PLATFORM_TELEMETRY" = "on" ]; then
  echo "platform telemetry: on"
fi

# ── The images nothing runs anymore ──────────────────────────────────────────
# Every deploy pulls three images tagged with their commit, and the box never
# needs an old set again: the registry keeps every tag, so a rollback re-pulls
# whatever it names. Left alone they only accumulate — 21 GB of them by
# 2026-08-17, 90% of everything docker held — and the only question about an
# unbounded pile is which day it fills the disk. Pruned only here, after the
# new containers are up and healthy, and prune
# never touches an image a container is using — so what is running, including
# everything a `deploy.sh <ref>` rollback would stop, is never the thing
# removed.
docker image prune -af
echo "pruned the images nothing runs"
LOCAL_COMPOSE_OVERRIDE
# The only part of hosted egma that is not in the public repository.
#
# `deploy.sh` is the normal entry point. It enables the
# `platform-telemetry` profile only when EGMA_TELEMETRY is `on`.
#
# Everything egma is comes from the first two files, under review and under
# `deployment.test.ts`. This third file holds the two things that are ours
# alone, and nothing else. **If something can go in the public files, it goes
# there** — that is the rule that broke when the box ran a whole hand-written
# compose file and drifted a day behind a rename.

services:
  # **The certificate, and the one line that makes it count.**
  #
  # Supabase signs its pooler with its own private CA — `*.pooler.supabase.com`
  # → `Supabase Intermediate 2021 CA` → `Supabase Root 2021 CA` — and that root
  # is in no public trust store. `pg` 8.22 verifies the chain where older
  # versions shrugged, so without this the API dies at boot reporting a
  # self-signed chain rather than a missing certificate.
  #
  # The alternative is `sslmode=no-verify`, and it is not an alternative. It
  # turns a verified connection into a merely encrypted one, and what that
  # protects is `EGMA_ENCRYPTION_KEY`'s work: the sealed **connection**
  # credentials of every customer. An encrypted connection to an attacker is
  # still a connection to an attacker.
  #
  # `deploy.sh` fetches the certificate before this file is ever read. Its
  # address is in the `egma/db/supabase` secret under `ca_url`.
  # **`image:` is the second thing this file is for.** egma's own compose file
  # builds all three services from source, which is right for a self-hoster and
  # wrong here: CI already built these, pushed them to ECR, and the box has a
  # read-only pull credential on purpose. Naming the image makes `pull` fetch
  # what CI made instead of the box compiling it again on a t3.large.
  #
  # `deploy.sh` appends EGMA_REGISTRY and EGMA_IMAGE_TAG to .env, so a run by
  # hand afterwards resolves to exactly what the deployment resolved to.
  api:
    image: ${EGMA_REGISTRY}/egma/api:${EGMA_IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
    # **Every container's log carries its own name, and is kept from eating
    # the disk.** The json-file driver's `labels` option writes the named
    # labels into each line's `attrs`, and compose already labels every
    # container with its project and service — so the collector below can
    # reject another Compose stack even if it also has a service named `api`.
    # The size cap is the other
    # half: unbounded logs on a box with a fixed disk are a quiet outage on a
    # timer. One anchor, aliased onto every service in this file.
    logging: &egma-logging
      driver: json-file
      options:
        labels: com.docker.compose.project,com.docker.compose.service
        max-size: 50m
        max-file: "3"
    # **This box publishes nothing — not 22, not 80, not 443, not 3100.** The
    # public compose file publishes the API on the host, which is right for a
    # self-hoster who reaches it in a browser and wrong here: the tunnel dials
    # out and shares this container's network namespace, so it reaches the API
    # without any port being bound on the host at all.
    #
    # `!reset` is how a compose override clears a list. Plain `ports: []` would
    # merge and change nothing, which would leave 3100 bound and the security
    # group as the only thing between it and the subnet.
    ports: !reset []
    environment:
      NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS: /certs/supabase-ca.crt
    volumes:
      - ./certs:/certs:ro
      # **The write-ahead log, on a volume rather than in the container's own
      # writable layer.** Evidence is staged here on its way to the ingestion
      # bucket: records waiting to be grouped into a segment, and the identity
      # of a sealed segment whose upload was not confirmed. The bucket is the
      # acknowledgement boundary, so nothing in here has been promised to a
      # customer yet — but an API replaced without this line comes back with
      # nothing to recover, which loses the staged records and lets a repeated
      # upload invent a second object instead of reaching for the first.
      # `docker compose down` keeps this volume unless an operator also passes
      # -v.
      #
      # It shares the box's root disk with everything else, which the
      # egma-box-disk alarm watches at 85%. egma's own
      # EGMA_INGESTION_LOG_MAX_BYTES default is 512 MiB and sits far under
      # that; raising it here without moving the alarm turns a bounded log
      # into a full disk.
      - api-ingestion:/var/lib/egma/ingestion

  # The grader reaches the same database and needs the same root.
  grader:
    image: ${EGMA_REGISTRY}/egma/grader:${EGMA_IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
    logging: *egma-logging
    environment:
      NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS: /certs/supabase-ca.crt
    volumes:
      - ./certs:/certs:ro

  # It reaches the API and the media bridge, not the database, so it needs no
  # certificate — only the image pin.
  simulator:
    image: ${EGMA_REGISTRY}/egma/simulator:${EGMA_IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
    logging: *egma-logging

  # **The only thing that faces the internet, and it faces it by dialling out.**
  # No `ports:` line appears anywhere in this deployment, and the box publishes
  # nothing at all — not 22, not 80, not 443.
  #
  # It shares the API container's network namespace rather than sitting beside
  # it on the compose network. That is what makes `http://localhost:3100` — the
  # origin the Cloudflare dashboard writes unless told otherwise — actually
  # true. Beside the API, `localhost` would be the tunnel itself, every request
  # would 502, and the log would blame an origin that is perfectly healthy.
  #
  # The cost of that choice, which is worth knowing before restarting anything:
  # restarting the API restarts the tunnel too, so it is a brief outage of the
  # whole address rather than of the API alone.
  # **Pinned by digest, like every other third-party image egma runs.** It was
  # on `:latest` until 2026-08-15, which made the one internet-facing component
  # of this deployment the only one a `docker compose pull` could change under
  # us. egma pins postgres, clickhouse, livekit, livekit-sip and redis; this was
  # the exception, and it was the worst one to make.
  #
  # To move it: pull the new tag, read its digest, put the digest here, deploy.
  tunnel:
    image: cloudflare/cloudflared@sha256:0aa26e284f05e6c77ae375b8c9c11d9eb6a448fb7bcd8d40f31cb6176189eb38
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: "service:api"
    command: ["tunnel", "--no-autoupdate", "run", "--token", "${CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_TOKEN}"]
    env_file: [.env]
    logging: *egma-logging
    depends_on:
      api:
        condition: service_healthy

  # **The one reader of everything above, and the only path telemetry leaves
  # this box on.** The api and grader send their own spans here (that is what
  # `EGMA_TELEMETRY_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://otel-collector:4318` in settings.map
  # points at), it tails this Compose project's application logs straight off
  # the Docker daemon's files — the tunnel's included, which no in-process
  # exporter could ever see — and it reads this project's container vitals and
  # the host vitals. Spans and logs go to
  # PostHog; the vitals go to CloudWatch, where the alarms live, over the
  # instance role like every other AWS call this box makes.
  #
  # It publishes nothing, like everything else here: port 4318 answers on the
  # compose network only, and everything outbound is the collector dialling
  # out. The egma containers keep working exactly as before if it dies —
  # telemetry is fire-and-forget from their side, and a broken collector costs
  # observations, never conversations.
  #
  # Root, and three sensitive mounts, knowingly: the daemon's log files and
  # the Docker socket are root's, and /hostfs is what lets it report the
  # box's own memory and disk rather than its container's. The socket is
  # root-equivalent on this machine — acceptable for a container whose config
  # is in this repository, whose image is pinned by digest below, and which
  # reaches nothing that was not already this box's to read.
  #
  # Pinned by digest, like the tunnel above and for the tunnel's reason. To
  # move it: pull the new tag, read its digest, put the digest here, deploy.
  otel-collector:
    # deploy.sh maps the same flag the api, grader, and pages read to this
    # profile. With the flag off, it also removes an older running collector,
    # so changing on to off stops logs and metrics leaving the box.
    profiles: [platform-telemetry]
    image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib@sha256:c5918f78992ee73b0d6f0e599423ac5ec52dd5d9726733114d6eca53d5a32ed5
    restart: unless-stopped
    user: "0"
    command: ["--config=/etc/egma/otel-collector.yaml"]
    environment:
      EGMA_POSTHOG_KEY: ${EGMA_POSTHOG_KEY:-}
      EGMA_POSTHOG_HOST: ${EGMA_POSTHOG_HOST:-}
      EGMA_DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT: ${EGMA_DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT:-production}
      EGMA_SERVICE_VERSION: ${EGMA_IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
      # 80% of the collector's 500 MiB memory limit, matching the limiter in
      # otel-collector.yaml. The two limits prevent an outage queue from
      # competing with the product containers for the box's memory.
      GOMEMLIMIT: 400MiB
    mem_limit: 500m
    volumes:
      # Relative to /opt/egma — deploy.sh anchors every path with
      # --project-directory, and this directory is synced from S3 on every
      # deploy, so the config can never drift from this repository.
      - ./deployment/otel-collector.yaml:/etc/egma/otel-collector.yaml:ro
      - /var/lib/docker/containers:/var/lib/docker/containers:ro
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
      - /:/hostfs:ro
      - otel-collector-storage:/var/lib/otelcol
    logging: *egma-logging

volumes:
  # Evidence on its way to the ingestion bucket: what a restarted API comes
  # back to, and the sealed identities that keep a retried upload reaching for
  # the object it already made.
  api-ingestion:
  # File offsets and queued PostHog batches survive collector replacements.
  # `docker compose down` keeps this volume unless an operator also passes -v.
  otel-collector-storage:

#!/bin/bash
# Turn settings.map into the .env the platform runs on.
#
#   ./assemble-env.sh [output-path] [path-to-egma-checkout]
#
# Replaces the hand-written fetch-env.sh that used to live on the box. That file
# was maintained separately from the code, drifted behind a rename, and took the
# platform's persona down with it. Nothing here is maintained separately: the
# list of settings comes from egma's own compose files and the answers come from
# settings.map, which check-settings.sh proves covers them.
#
# **It refuses to write anything if the check fails.** A half-answered .env is
# the failure this whole arrangement exists to prevent, so a gap stops the
# deployment rather than reaching it.
#
# **No secret value is written anywhere but the output file**, which is created
# with mode 600. Nothing is echoed, and a secret is fetched once however many
# settings read from it.
set -euo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
OUT="${1:-/opt/egma/.env}"
CODE="${2:-$(cd "$HERE/../../.." && pwd)}"
REGION="${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}"

bash "$HERE/check-settings.sh" "$CODE" || {
  echo >&2
  echo "Refusing to assemble a .env that does not answer every setting." >&2
  exit 1
}

umask 077
tmp="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT

declare -A cache

fetch() {
  local id="$1"
  [ -n "${cache[$id]+set}" ] || cache[$id]="$(aws secretsmanager get-secret-value \
    --secret-id "$id" --region "$REGION" --query SecretString --output text)"
  printf '%s' "${cache[$id]}"
}

field() {
  python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.loads(sys.argv[1])[sys.argv[2]])' "$1" "$2"
}

written=0
while read -r name how a b _rest; do
  case "$how" in
    secret)
      value="$(field "$(fetch "$a")" "$b")"
      printf '%s=%s\n' "$name" "$value" >> "$tmp"
      written=$((written + 1))
      ;;
    literal|inert)
      # inert writes exactly like literal — the difference is what it tells a
      # reader of the map: this value feeds a profiled-out container that never
      # starts, and exists only because compose checks `:?` markers for every
      # service at file load, switched-off ones included.
      printf '%s=%s\n' "$name" "$a" >> "$tmp"
      written=$((written + 1))
      ;;
    deploy-time)
      # deploy.sh appends these after this script runs, because they describe
      # the deployment being made rather than the platform being deployed.
      ;;
    compose-default|unset)
      # Deliberately absent, so egma's own default applies. Writing an empty
      # value here would not be the same thing: compose passes an unset
      # optional through as an empty string, and the API treats "" and "never
      # set" alike only because it filters blanks out again on the way in.
      ;;
    *)
      echo "settings.map: $name has an unknown disposition '$how'" >&2
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac
done < <(grep -vE '^\s*(#|$)' "$HERE/settings.map")

install -m 600 "$tmp" "$OUT"
echo "assembled $written settings into $OUT"
",
    "Error": ""
}

# ## The layout, and the rule behind it
#
#   /opt/egma/deployment/   this directory. Synced from S3 with --delete on
#                           every deploy, so nothing in it can drift — it IS
#                           the egma-cloud repository's deployment/ folder
#   /opt/egma/egma/         egma's own repository, checked out at the ref
#                           being deployed. Rebuilt whenever it is missing
#   /opt/egma/certs/        the Supabase root, fetched when missing
#   /opt/egma/.env          assembled fresh on every deploy, root-only
#
# Nothing under /opt/egma is authored on the box. Every file either arrives
# from a repository (via S3 or git) or is derived at deploy time. That rule is
# the fix for 2026-08-15, when hand-written files on this box drifted behind a
# rename in the code and took the persona's settings down silently.
set -euo pipefail

REF="${1:-latest}"
REGION="${AWS_REGION:-${AWS_DEFAULT_REGION:-us-east-1}}"
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
WORK="$(cd "$HERE/.." && pwd)"
CODE="$WORK/egma"

# ── egma's own files, at the commit the images were built from ───────────────
# The compose files and the images must come from one commit. Deploying an
# image built from one tree with compose files from another is how a setting
# goes missing without anything failing.
if [ -d "$CODE/.git" ]; then
  git -C "$CODE" fetch --tags --quiet origin
else
  git clone --quiet https://github.com/egma-ai/egma.git "$CODE"
fi
if git -C "$CODE" rev-parse --verify --quiet "$REF^{commit}" >/dev/null; then
  git -C "$CODE" checkout --quiet --detach "$REF"
  echo "egma files at $REF ($(git -C "$CODE" rev-parse --short HEAD))"
else
  git -C "$CODE" checkout --quiet --detach origin/main
  echo "no ref '$REF' in the repository; using origin/main for the compose files"
fi

# ── The Supabase root ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Fetched rather than committed: it is a published file, and its address is in
# the egma/db/supabase secret under ca_url. Without it the API dies at boot
# reporting a self-signed chain.
if [ ! -s "$WORK/certs/supabase-ca.crt" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$WORK/certs"
  curl -fsSL \
    "$(aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id egma/db/supabase \
        --region "$REGION" --query SecretString --output text \
      | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["ca_url"])')" \
    -o "$WORK/certs/supabase-ca.crt"
  echo "fetched the Supabase root certificate"
fi

# ── The settings ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Assembled fresh every time, so changing a secret and deploying is enough.
# assemble-env.sh refuses to write anything if settings.map does not answer
# every setting egma's compose files ask for — a gap stops the deployment here
# rather than reaching production.
bash "$HERE/assemble-env.sh" "$WORK/.env" "$CODE"

ACCOUNT="$(aws sts get-caller-identity --query Account --output text)"
REGISTRY="${EGMA_REGISTRY:-${ACCOUNT}.dkr.ecr.${REGION}.amazonaws.com}"

# The registry and tag join the assembled settings rather than being exported,
# so a `docker compose` run by hand afterwards sees exactly what the deployment
# saw rather than resolving to something else.
printf 'EGMA_REGISTRY=%s\nEGMA_IMAGE_TAG=%s\n' "$REGISTRY" "$REF" >> "$WORK/.env"

# One flag controls every platform telemetry path. The api and grader read it
# themselves. The collector is a Compose profile, so this deployment maps the
# same value to that profile. Anything but `on`, including an absent value,
# also removes a collector left running by an earlier enabled deployment.
PLATFORM_TELEMETRY="$(awk -F= '
  $1 == "EGMA_TELEMETRY" {
    value = substr($0, index($0, "=") + 1)
    gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", value)
    print tolower(value)
    exit
  }
' "$WORK/.env")"

COMPOSE_PROFILE_ARGS=()
if [ "$PLATFORM_TELEMETRY" = "on" ]; then
  COMPOSE_PROFILE_ARGS=(--profile platform-telemetry)
fi

# --project-directory anchors every relative path in the stack — ./certs, the
# env_file — to /opt/egma, whichever file names it.
compose() {
  docker compose \
    -f "$CODE/docker-compose.yml" \
    -f "$CODE/docker-compose.managed.yml" \
    -f "$HERE/local.yml" \
    --project-directory "$WORK" \
    --project-name egma "${COMPOSE_PROFILE_ARGS[@]}" "$@"
}

# Activate the collector profile only for this cleanup command. Stop and
# remove it before the rest of the deploy when the flag is off. A failed
# removal stops the deploy; it must not say telemetry is off while an old
# collector still sends data.
if [ "$PLATFORM_TELEMETRY" != "on" ]; then
  compose --profile platform-telemetry rm --stop --force otel-collector
  echo "platform telemetry: off"
fi

aws ecr get-login-password --region "$REGION" \
  | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin "$REGISTRY"

# `--no-build` matters: egma's compose file builds all three services from
# source, which is right for a self-hoster and wrong here. CI built these
# already, and this box holds a read-only pull credential on purpose.
compose pull
compose up -d --wait --wait-timeout 300 --no-build
compose ps
if [ "$PLATFORM_TELEMETRY" = "on" ]; then
  echo "platform telemetry: on"
fi

# ── The images nothing runs anymore ──────────────────────────────────────────
# Every deploy pulls three images tagged with their commit, and the box never
# needs an old set again: the registry keeps every tag, so a rollback re-pulls
# whatever it names. Left alone they only accumulate — 21 GB of them by
# 2026-08-17, 90% of everything docker held — and the only question about an
# unbounded pile is which day it fills the disk. Pruned only here, after the
# new containers are up and healthy, and prune
# never touches an image a container is using — so what is running, including
# everything a `deploy.sh <ref>` rollback would stop, is never the thing
# removed.
docker image prune -af
echo "pruned the images nothing runs"
LOCAL_COMPOSE_OVERRIDE
# The only part of hosted egma that is not in the public repository.
#
# `deploy.sh` is the normal entry point. It enables the
# `platform-telemetry` profile only when EGMA_TELEMETRY is `on`.
#
# Everything egma is comes from the first two files, under review and under
# `deployment.test.ts`. This third file holds the two things that are ours
# alone, and nothing else. **If something can go in the public files, it goes
# there** — that is the rule that broke when the box ran a whole hand-written
# compose file and drifted a day behind a rename.

services:
  # **The certificate, and the one line that makes it count.**
  #
  # Supabase signs its pooler with its own private CA — `*.pooler.supabase.com`
  # → `Supabase Intermediate 2021 CA` → `Supabase Root 2021 CA` — and that root
  # is in no public trust store. `pg` 8.22 verifies the chain where older
  # versions shrugged, so without this the API dies at boot reporting a
  # self-signed chain rather than a missing certificate.
  #
  # The alternative is `sslmode=no-verify`, and it is not an alternative. It
  # turns a verified connection into a merely encrypted one, and what that
  # protects is `EGMA_ENCRYPTION_KEY`'s work: the sealed **connection**
  # credentials of every customer. An encrypted connection to an attacker is
  # still a connection to an attacker.
  #
  # `deploy.sh` fetches the certificate before this file is ever read. Its
  # address is in the `egma/db/supabase` secret under `ca_url`.
  # **`image:` is the second thing this file is for.** egma's own compose file
  # builds all three services from source, which is right for a self-hoster and
  # wrong here: CI already built these, pushed them to ECR, and the box has a
  # read-only pull credential on purpose. Naming the image makes `pull` fetch
  # what CI made instead of the box compiling it again on a t3.large.
  #
  # `deploy.sh` appends EGMA_REGISTRY and EGMA_IMAGE_TAG to .env, so a run by
  # hand afterwards resolves to exactly what the deployment resolved to.
  api:
    image: ${EGMA_REGISTRY}/egma/api:${EGMA_IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
    # **Every container's log carries its own name, and is kept from eating
    # the disk.** The json-file driver's `labels` option writes the named
    # labels into each line's `attrs`, and compose already labels every
    # container with its project and service — so the collector below can
    # reject another Compose stack even if it also has a service named `api`.
    # The size cap is the other
    # half: unbounded logs on a box with a fixed disk are a quiet outage on a
    # timer. One anchor, aliased onto every service in this file.
    logging: &egma-logging
      driver: json-file
      options:
        labels: com.docker.compose.project,com.docker.compose.service
        max-size: 50m
        max-file: "3"
    # **This box publishes nothing — not 22, not 80, not 443, not 3100.** The
    # public compose file publishes the API on the host, which is right for a
    # self-hoster who reaches it in a browser and wrong here: the tunnel dials
    # out and shares this container's network namespace, so it reaches the API
    # without any port being bound on the host at all.
    #
    # `!reset` is how a compose override clears a list. Plain `ports: []` would
    # merge and change nothing, which would leave 3100 bound and the security
    # group as the only thing between it and the subnet.
    ports: !reset []
    environment:
      NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS: /certs/supabase-ca.crt
    volumes:
      - ./certs:/certs:ro
      # **The write-ahead log, on a volume rather than in the container's own
      # writable layer.** Evidence is staged here on its way to the ingestion
      # bucket: records waiting to be grouped into a segment, and the identity
      # of a sealed segment whose upload was not confirmed. The bucket is the
      # acknowledgement boundary, so nothing in here has been promised to a
      # customer yet — but an API replaced without this line comes back with
      # nothing to recover, which loses the staged records and lets a repeated
      # upload invent a second object instead of reaching for the first.
      # `docker compose down` keeps this volume unless an operator also passes
      # -v.
      #
      # It shares the box's root disk with everything else, which the
      # egma-box-disk alarm watches at 85%. egma's own
      # EGMA_INGESTION_LOG_MAX_BYTES default is 512 MiB and sits far under
      # that; raising it here without moving the alarm turns a bounded log
      # into a full disk.
      - api-ingestion:/var/lib/egma/ingestion

  # The grader reaches the same database and needs the same root.
  grader:
    image: ${EGMA_REGISTRY}/egma/grader:${EGMA_IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
    logging: *egma-logging
    environment:
      NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS: /certs/supabase-ca.crt
    volumes:
      - ./certs:/certs:ro

  # It reaches the API and the media bridge, not the database, so it needs no
  # certificate — only the image pin.
  simulator:
    image: ${EGMA_REGISTRY}/egma/simulator:${EGMA_IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
    logging: *egma-logging

  # **The only thing that faces the internet, and it faces it by dialling out.**
  # No `ports:` line appears anywhere in this deployment, and the box publishes
  # nothing at all — not 22, not 80, not 443.
  #
  # It shares the API container's network namespace rather than sitting beside
  # it on the compose network. That is what makes `http://localhost:3100` — the
  # origin the Cloudflare dashboard writes unless told otherwise — actually
  # true. Beside the API, `localhost` would be the tunnel itself, every request
  # would 502, and the log would blame an origin that is perfectly healthy.
  #
  # The cost of that choice, which is worth knowing before restarting anything:
  # restarting the API restarts the tunnel too, so it is a brief outage of the
  # whole address rather than of the API alone.
  # **Pinned by digest, like every other third-party image egma runs.** It was
  # on `:latest` until 2026-08-15, which made the one internet-facing component
  # of this deployment the only one a `docker compose pull` could change under
  # us. egma pins postgres, clickhouse, livekit, livekit-sip and redis; this was
  # the exception, and it was the worst one to make.
  #
  # To move it: pull the new tag, read its digest, put the digest here, deploy.
  tunnel:
    image: cloudflare/cloudflared@sha256:0aa26e284f05e6c77ae375b8c9c11d9eb6a448fb7bcd8d40f31cb6176189eb38
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: "service:api"
    command: ["tunnel", "--no-autoupdate", "run", "--token", "${CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_TOKEN}"]
    env_file: [.env]
    logging: *egma-logging
    depends_on:
      api:
        condition: service_healthy

  # **The one reader of everything above, and the only path telemetry leaves
  # this box on.** The api and grader send their own spans here (that is what
  # `EGMA_TELEMETRY_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://otel-collector:4318` in settings.map
  # points at), it tails this Compose project's application logs straight off
  # the Docker daemon's files — the tunnel's included, which no in-process
  # exporter could ever see — and it reads this project's container vitals and
  # the host vitals. Spans and logs go to
  # PostHog; the vitals go to CloudWatch, where the alarms live, over the
  # instance role like every other AWS call this box makes.
  #
  # It publishes nothing, like everything else here: port 4318 answers on the
  # compose network only, and everything outbound is the collector dialling
  # out. The egma containers keep working exactly as before if it dies —
  # telemetry is fire-and-forget from their side, and a broken collector costs
  # observations, never conversations.
  #
  # Root, and three sensitive mounts, knowingly: the daemon's log files and
  # the Docker socket are root's, and /hostfs is what lets it report the
  # box's own memory and disk rather than its container's. The socket is
  # root-equivalent on this machine — acceptable for a container whose config
  # is in this repository, whose image is pinned by digest below, and which
  # reaches nothing that was not already this box's to read.
  #
  # Pinned by digest, like the tunnel above and for the tunnel's reason. To
  # move it: pull the new tag, read its digest, put the digest here, deploy.
  otel-collector:
    # deploy.sh maps the same flag the api, grader, and pages read to this
    # profile. With the flag off, it also removes an older running collector,
    # so changing on to off stops logs and metrics leaving the box.
    profiles: [platform-telemetry]
    image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib@sha256:c5918f78992ee73b0d6f0e599423ac5ec52dd5d9726733114d6eca53d5a32ed5
    restart: unless-stopped
    user: "0"
    command: ["--config=/etc/egma/otel-collector.yaml"]
    environment:
      EGMA_POSTHOG_KEY: ${EGMA_POSTHOG_KEY:-}
      EGMA_POSTHOG_HOST: ${EGMA_POSTHOG_HOST:-}
      EGMA_DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT: ${EGMA_DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT:-production}
      EGMA_SERVICE_VERSION: ${EGMA_IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
      # 80% of the collector's 500 MiB memory limit, matching the limiter in
      # otel-collector.yaml. The two limits prevent an outage queue from
      # competing with the product containers for the box's memory.
      GOMEMLIMIT: 400MiB
    mem_limit: 500m
    volumes:
      # Relative to /opt/egma — deploy.sh anchors every path with
      # --project-directory, and this directory is synced from S3 on every
      # deploy, so the config can never drift from this repository.
      - ./deployment/otel-collector.yaml:/etc/egma/otel-collector.yaml:ro
      - /var/lib/docker/containers:/var/lib/docker/containers:ro
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
      - /:/hostfs:ro
      - otel-collector-storage:/var/lib/otelcol
    logging: *egma-logging

volumes:
  # Evidence on its way to the ingestion bucket: what a restarted API comes
  # back to, and the sealed identities that keep a retried upload reaching for
  # the object it already made.
  api-ingestion:
  # File offsets and queued PostHog batches survive collector replacements.
  # `docker compose down` keeps this volume unless an operator also passes -v.
  otel-collector-storage:
ASSEMBLE_ENV_STRUCTURE
#!/bin/bash
# Turn settings.map into the .env the platform runs on.
#
#   ./assemble-env.sh [output-path] [path-to-egma-checkout]
#
# Replaces the hand-written fetch-env.sh that used to live on the box. That file
# was maintained separately from the code, drifted behind a rename, and took the
# platform's persona down with it. Nothing here is maintained separately: the
# list of settings comes from egma's own compose files and the answers come from
# settings.map, which check-settings.sh proves covers them.
#
# **It refuses to write anything if the check fails.** A half-answered .env is
# the failure this whole arrangement exists to prevent, so a gap stops the
# deployment rather than reaching it.
#
# **No secret value is written anywhere but the output file**, which is created
# with mode 600. Nothing is echoed, and a secret is fetched once however many
# settings read from it.
set -euo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
OUT="${1:-/opt/egma/.env}"
CODE="${2:-$(cd "$HERE/../../.." && pwd)}"
REGION="${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}"

bash "$HERE/check-settings.sh" "$CODE" || {
  echo >&2
  echo "Refusing to assemble a .env that does not answer every setting." >&2
  exit 1
}

umask 077
tmp="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT

declare -A cache

fetch() {
  local id="$1"
  [ -n "${cache[$id]+set}" ] || cache[$id]="$(aws secretsmanager get-secret-value \
    --secret-id "$id" --region "$REGION" --query SecretString --output text)"
  printf '%s' "${cache[$id]}"
}

field() {
  python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.loads(sys.argv[1])[sys.argv[2]])' "$1" "$2"
}

written=0
while read -r name how a b _rest; do
  case "$how" in
    secret)
      value="$(field "$(fetch "$a")" "$b")"
      printf '%s=%s\n' "$name" "$value" >> "$tmp"
      written=$((written + 1))
      ;;
    literal|inert)
      # inert writes exactly like literal — the difference is what it tells a
      # reader of the map: this value feeds a profiled-out container that never
      # starts, and exists only because compose checks `:?` markers for every
      # service at file load, switched-off ones included.
      printf '%s=%s\n' "$name" "$a" >> "$tmp"
      written=$((written + 1))
      ;;
    deploy-time)
      # deploy.sh appends these after this script runs, because they describe
      # the deployment being made rather than the platform being deployed.
      ;;
    compose-default|unset)
      # Deliberately absent, so egma's own default applies. Writing an empty
      # value here would not be the same thing: compose passes an unset
      # optional through as an empty string, and the API treats "" and "never
      # set" alike only because it filters blanks out again on the way in.
      ;;
    *)
      echo "settings.map: $name has an unknown disposition '$how'" >&2
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac
done < <(grep -vE '^\s*(#|$)' "$HERE/settings.map")

install -m 600 "$tmp" "$OUT"
echo "assembled $written settings into $OUT"
",
    "Error": ""
}

#!/bin/bash
# Replace what the platform box is running with a named build.
#
#   /opt/egma/deployment/deploy.sh <ref>
#
# The deploy workflow in the public repository invokes this over SSM, after
# syncing this whole directory fresh from S3. It is equally a script to run by
# hand on the box when nobody wants to drive a deployment through CI.
#
# ## The layout, and the rule behind it
#
#   /opt/egma/deployment/   this directory. Synced from S3 with --delete on
#                           every deploy, so nothing in it can drift — it IS
#                           the egma-cloud repository's deployment/ folder
#   /opt/egma/egma/         egma's own repository, checked out at the ref
#                           being deployed. Rebuilt whenever it is missing
#   /opt/egma/certs/        the Supabase root, fetched when missing
#   /opt/egma/.env          assembled fresh on every deploy, root-only
#
# Nothing under /opt/egma is authored on the box. Every file either arrives
# from a repository (via S3 or git) or is derived at deploy time. That rule is
# the fix for 2026-08-15, when hand-written files on this box drifted behind a
# rename in the code and took the persona's settings down silently.
set -euo pipefail

REF="${1:-latest}"
REGION="${AWS_REGION:-${AWS_DEFAULT_REGION:-us-east-1}}"
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
WORK="$(cd "$HERE/.." && pwd)"
CODE="$WORK/egma"

# ── egma's own files, at the commit the images were built from ───────────────
# The compose files and the images must come from one commit. Deploying an
# image built from one tree with compose files from another is how a setting
# goes missing without anything failing.
if [ -d "$CODE/.git" ]; then
  git -C "$CODE" fetch --tags --quiet origin
else
  git clone --quiet https://github.com/egma-ai/egma.git "$CODE"
fi
if git -C "$CODE" rev-parse --verify --quiet "$REF^{commit}" >/dev/null; then
  git -C "$CODE" checkout --quiet --detach "$REF"
  echo "egma files at $REF ($(git -C "$CODE" rev-parse --short HEAD))"
else
  git -C "$CODE" checkout --quiet --detach origin/main
  echo "no ref '$REF' in the repository; using origin/main for the compose files"
fi

# ── The Supabase root ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Fetched rather than committed: it is a published file, and its address is in
# the egma/db/supabase secret under ca_url. Without it the API dies at boot
# reporting a self-signed chain.
if [ ! -s "$WORK/certs/supabase-ca.crt" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$WORK/certs"
  curl -fsSL \
    "$(aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id egma/db/supabase \
        --region "$REGION" --query SecretString --output text \
      | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["ca_url"])')" \
    -o "$WORK/certs/supabase-ca.crt"
  echo "fetched the Supabase root certificate"
fi

# ── The settings ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Assembled fresh every time, so changing a secret and deploying is enough.
# assemble-env.sh refuses to write anything if settings.map does not answer
# every setting egma's compose files ask for — a gap stops the deployment here
# rather than reaching production.
bash "$HERE/assemble-env.sh" "$WORK/.env" "$CODE"

ACCOUNT="$(aws sts get-caller-identity --query Account --output text)"
REGISTRY="${EGMA_REGISTRY:-${ACCOUNT}.dkr.ecr.${REGION}.amazonaws.com}"

# The registry and tag join the assembled settings rather than being exported,
# so a `docker compose` run by hand afterwards sees exactly what the deployment
# saw rather than resolving to something else.
printf 'EGMA_REGISTRY=%s\nEGMA_IMAGE_TAG=%s\n' "$REGISTRY" "$REF" >> "$WORK/.env"

# One flag controls every platform telemetry path. The api and grader read it
# themselves. The collector is a Compose profile, so this deployment maps the
# same value to that profile. Anything but `on`, including an absent value,
# also removes a collector left running by an earlier enabled deployment.
PLATFORM_TELEMETRY="$(awk -F= '
  $1 == "EGMA_TELEMETRY" {
    value = substr($0, index($0, "=") + 1)
    gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", value)
    print tolower(value)
    exit
  }
' "$WORK/.env")"

COMPOSE_PROFILE_ARGS=()
if [ "$PLATFORM_TELEMETRY" = "on" ]; then
  COMPOSE_PROFILE_ARGS=(--profile platform-telemetry)
fi

# --project-directory anchors every relative path in the stack — ./certs, the
# env_file — to /opt/egma, whichever file names it.
compose() {
  docker compose \
    -f "$CODE/docker-compose.yml" \
    -f "$CODE/docker-compose.managed.yml" \
    -f "$HERE/local.yml" \
    --project-directory "$WORK" \
    --project-name egma "${COMPOSE_PROFILE_ARGS[@]}" "$@"
}

# Activate the collector profile only for this cleanup command. Stop and
# remove it before the rest of the deploy when the flag is off. A failed
# removal stops the deploy; it must not say telemetry is off while an old
# collector still sends data.
if [ "$PLATFORM_TELEMETRY" != "on" ]; then
  compose --profile platform-telemetry rm --stop --force otel-collector
  echo "platform telemetry: off"
fi

aws ecr get-login-password --region "$REGION" \
  | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin "$REGISTRY"

# `--no-build` matters: egma's compose file builds all three services from
# source, which is right for a self-hoster and wrong here. CI built these
# already, and this box holds a read-only pull credential on purpose.
compose pull
compose up -d --wait --wait-timeout 300 --no-build
compose ps
if [ "$PLATFORM_TELEMETRY" = "on" ]; then
  echo "platform telemetry: on"
fi

# ── The images nothing runs anymore ──────────────────────────────────────────
# Every deploy pulls three images tagged with their commit, and the box never
# needs an old set again: the registry keeps every tag, so a rollback re-pulls
# whatever it names. Left alone they only accumulate — 21 GB of them by
# 2026-08-17, 90% of everything docker held — and the only question about an
# unbounded pile is which day it fills the disk. Pruned only here, after the
# new containers are up and healthy, and prune
# never touches an image a container is using — so what is running, including
# everything a `deploy.sh <ref>` rollback would stop, is never the thing
# removed.
docker image prune -af
echo "pruned the images nothing runs"
LOCAL_COMPOSE_OVERRIDE
# The only part of hosted egma that is not in the public repository.
#
# `deploy.sh` is the normal entry point. It enables the
# `platform-telemetry` profile only when EGMA_TELEMETRY is `on`.
#
# Everything egma is comes from the first two files, under review and under
# `deployment.test.ts`. This third file holds the two things that are ours
# alone, and nothing else. **If something can go in the public files, it goes
# there** — that is the rule that broke when the box ran a whole hand-written
# compose file and drifted a day behind a rename.

services:
  # **The certificate, and the one line that makes it count.**
  #
  # Supabase signs its pooler with its own private CA — `*.pooler.supabase.com`
  # → `Supabase Intermediate 2021 CA` → `Supabase Root 2021 CA` — and that root
  # is in no public trust store. `pg` 8.22 verifies the chain where older
  # versions shrugged, so without this the API dies at boot reporting a
  # self-signed chain rather than a missing certificate.
  #
  # The alternative is `sslmode=no-verify`, and it is not an alternative. It
  # turns a verified connection into a merely encrypted one, and what that
  # protects is `EGMA_ENCRYPTION_KEY`'s work: the sealed **connection**
  # credentials of every customer. An encrypted connection to an attacker is
  # still a connection to an attacker.
  #
  # `deploy.sh` fetches the certificate before this file is ever read. Its
  # address is in the `egma/db/supabase` secret under `ca_url`.
  # **`image:` is the second thing this file is for.** egma's own compose file
  # builds all three services from source, which is right for a self-hoster and
  # wrong here: CI already built these, pushed them to ECR, and the box has a
  # read-only pull credential on purpose. Naming the image makes `pull` fetch
  # what CI made instead of the box compiling it again on a t3.large.
  #
  # `deploy.sh` appends EGMA_REGISTRY and EGMA_IMAGE_TAG to .env, so a run by
  # hand afterwards resolves to exactly what the deployment resolved to.
  api:
    image: ${EGMA_REGISTRY}/egma/api:${EGMA_IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
    # **Every container's log carries its own name, and is kept from eating
    # the disk.** The json-file driver's `labels` option writes the named
    # labels into each line's `attrs`, and compose already labels every
    # container with its project and service — so the collector below can
    # reject another Compose stack even if it also has a service named `api`.
    # The size cap is the other
    # half: unbounded logs on a box with a fixed disk are a quiet outage on a
    # timer. One anchor, aliased onto every service in this file.
    logging: &egma-logging
      driver: json-file
      options:
        labels: com.docker.compose.project,com.docker.compose.service
        max-size: 50m
        max-file: "3"
    # **This box publishes nothing — not 22, not 80, not 443, not 3100.** The
    # public compose file publishes the API on the host, which is right for a
    # self-hoster who reaches it in a browser and wrong here: the tunnel dials
    # out and shares this container's network namespace, so it reaches the API
    # without any port being bound on the host at all.
    #
    # `!reset` is how a compose override clears a list. Plain `ports: []` would
    # merge and change nothing, which would leave 3100 bound and the security
    # group as the only thing between it and the subnet.
    ports: !reset []
    environment:
      NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS: /certs/supabase-ca.crt
    volumes:
      - ./certs:/certs:ro
      # **The write-ahead log, on a volume rather than in the container's own
      # writable layer.** Evidence is staged here on its way to the ingestion
      # bucket: records waiting to be grouped into a segment, and the identity
      # of a sealed segment whose upload was not confirmed. The bucket is the
      # acknowledgement boundary, so nothing in here has been promised to a
      # customer yet — but an API replaced without this line comes back with
      # nothing to recover, which loses the staged records and lets a repeated
      # upload invent a second object instead of reaching for the first.
      # `docker compose down` keeps this volume unless an operator also passes
      # -v.
      #
      # It shares the box's root disk with everything else, which the
      # egma-box-disk alarm watches at 85%. egma's own
      # EGMA_INGESTION_LOG_MAX_BYTES default is 512 MiB and sits far under
      # that; raising it here without moving the alarm turns a bounded log
      # into a full disk.
      - api-ingestion:/var/lib/egma/ingestion

  # The grader reaches the same database and needs the same root.
  grader:
    image: ${EGMA_REGISTRY}/egma/grader:${EGMA_IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
    logging: *egma-logging
    environment:
      NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS: /certs/supabase-ca.crt
    volumes:
      - ./certs:/certs:ro

  # It reaches the API and the media bridge, not the database, so it needs no
  # certificate — only the image pin.
  simulator:
    image: ${EGMA_REGISTRY}/egma/simulator:${EGMA_IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
    logging: *egma-logging

  # **The only thing that faces the internet, and it faces it by dialling out.**
  # No `ports:` line appears anywhere in this deployment, and the box publishes
  # nothing at all — not 22, not 80, not 443.
  #
  # It shares the API container's network namespace rather than sitting beside
  # it on the compose network. That is what makes `http://localhost:3100` — the
  # origin the Cloudflare dashboard writes unless told otherwise — actually
  # true. Beside the API, `localhost` would be the tunnel itself, every request
  # would 502, and the log would blame an origin that is perfectly healthy.
  #
  # The cost of that choice, which is worth knowing before restarting anything:
  # restarting the API restarts the tunnel too, so it is a brief outage of the
  # whole address rather than of the API alone.
  # **Pinned by digest, like every other third-party image egma runs.** It was
  # on `:latest` until 2026-08-15, which made the one internet-facing component
  # of this deployment the only one a `docker compose pull` could change under
  # us. egma pins postgres, clickhouse, livekit, livekit-sip and redis; this was
  # the exception, and it was the worst one to make.
  #
  # To move it: pull the new tag, read its digest, put the digest here, deploy.
  tunnel:
    image: cloudflare/cloudflared@sha256:0aa26e284f05e6c77ae375b8c9c11d9eb6a448fb7bcd8d40f31cb6176189eb38
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: "service:api"
    command: ["tunnel", "--no-autoupdate", "run", "--token", "${CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_TOKEN}"]
    env_file: [.env]
    logging: *egma-logging
    depends_on:
      api:
        condition: service_healthy

  # **The one reader of everything above, and the only path telemetry leaves
  # this box on.** The api and grader send their own spans here (that is what
  # `EGMA_TELEMETRY_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://otel-collector:4318` in settings.map
  # points at), it tails this Compose project's application logs straight off
  # the Docker daemon's files — the tunnel's included, which no in-process
  # exporter could ever see — and it reads this project's container vitals and
  # the host vitals. Spans and logs go to
  # PostHog; the vitals go to CloudWatch, where the alarms live, over the
  # instance role like every other AWS call this box makes.
  #
  # It publishes nothing, like everything else here: port 4318 answers on the
  # compose network only, and everything outbound is the collector dialling
  # out. The egma containers keep working exactly as before if it dies —
  # telemetry is fire-and-forget from their side, and a broken collector costs
  # observations, never conversations.
  #
  # Root, and three sensitive mounts, knowingly: the daemon's log files and
  # the Docker socket are root's, and /hostfs is what lets it report the
  # box's own memory and disk rather than its container's. The socket is
  # root-equivalent on this machine — acceptable for a container whose config
  # is in this repository, whose image is pinned by digest below, and which
  # reaches nothing that was not already this box's to read.
  #
  # Pinned by digest, like the tunnel above and for the tunnel's reason. To
  # move it: pull the new tag, read its digest, put the digest here, deploy.
  otel-collector:
    # deploy.sh maps the same flag the api, grader, and pages read to this
    # profile. With the flag off, it also removes an older running collector,
    # so changing on to off stops logs and metrics leaving the box.
    profiles: [platform-telemetry]
    image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib@sha256:c5918f78992ee73b0d6f0e599423ac5ec52dd5d9726733114d6eca53d5a32ed5
    restart: unless-stopped
    user: "0"
    command: ["--config=/etc/egma/otel-collector.yaml"]
    environment:
      EGMA_POSTHOG_KEY: ${EGMA_POSTHOG_KEY:-}
      EGMA_POSTHOG_HOST: ${EGMA_POSTHOG_HOST:-}
      EGMA_DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT: ${EGMA_DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT:-production}
      EGMA_SERVICE_VERSION: ${EGMA_IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
      # 80% of the collector's 500 MiB memory limit, matching the limiter in
      # otel-collector.yaml. The two limits prevent an outage queue from
      # competing with the product containers for the box's memory.
      GOMEMLIMIT: 400MiB
    mem_limit: 500m
    volumes:
      # Relative to /opt/egma — deploy.sh anchors every path with
      # --project-directory, and this directory is synced from S3 on every
      # deploy, so the config can never drift from this repository.
      - ./deployment/otel-collector.yaml:/etc/egma/otel-collector.yaml:ro
      - /var/lib/docker/containers:/var/lib/docker/containers:ro
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
      - /:/hostfs:ro
      - otel-collector-storage:/var/lib/otelcol
    logging: *egma-logging

volumes:
  # Evidence on its way to the ingestion bucket: what a restarted API comes
  # back to, and the sealed identities that keep a retried upload reaching for
  # the object it already made.
  api-ingestion:
  # File offsets and queued PostHog batches survive collector replacements.
  # `docker compose down` keeps this volume unless an operator also passes -v.
  otel-collector-storage:
ASSEMBLE_ENV_STRUCTURE
#!/bin/bash
# Turn settings.map into the .env the platform runs on.
#
#   ./assemble-env.sh [output-path] [path-to-egma-checkout]
#
# Replaces the hand-written fetch-env.sh that used to live on the box. That file
# was maintained separately from the code, drifted behind a rename, and took the
# platform's persona down with it. Nothing here is maintained separately: the
# list of settings comes from egma's own compose files and the answers come from
# settings.map, which check-settings.sh proves covers them.
#
# **It refuses to write anything if the check fails.** A half-answered .env is
# the failure this whole arrangement exists to prevent, so a gap stops the
# deployment rather than reaching it.
#
# **No secret value is written anywhere but the output file**, which is created
# with mode 600. Nothing is echoed, and a secret is fetched once however many
# settings read from it.
set -euo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
OUT="${1:-/opt/egma/.env}"
CODE="${2:-$(cd "$HERE/../../.." && pwd)}"
REGION="${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}"

bash "$HERE/check-settings.sh" "$CODE" || {
  echo >&2
  echo "Refusing to assemble a .env that does not answer every setting." >&2
  exit 1
}

umask 077
tmp="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT

declare -A cache

fetch() {
  local id="$1"
  [ -n "${cache[$id]+set}" ] || cache[$id]="$(aws secretsmanager get-secret-value \
    --secret-id "$id" --region "$REGION" --query SecretString --output text)"
  printf '%s' "${cache[$id]}"
}

field() {
  python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.loads(sys.argv[1])[sys.argv[2]])' "$1" "$2"
}

written=0
while read -r name how a b _rest; do
  case "$how" in
    secret)
      value="$(field "$(fetch "$a")" "$b")"
      printf '%s=%s\n' "$name" "$value" >> "$tmp"
      written=$((written + 1))
      ;;
    literal|inert)
      # inert writes exactly like literal — the difference is what it tells a
      # reader of the map: this value feeds a profiled-out container that never
      # starts, and exists only because compose checks `:?` markers for every
      # service at file load, switched-off ones included.
      printf '%s=%s\n' "$name" "$a" >> "$tmp"
      written=$((written + 1))
      ;;
    deploy-time)
      # deploy.sh appends these after this script runs, because they describe
      # the deployment being made rather than the platform being deployed.
      ;;
    compose-default|unset)
      # Deliberately absent, so egma's own default applies. Writing an empty
      # value here would not be the same thing: compose passes an unset
      # optional through as an empty string, and the API treats "" and "never
      # set" alike only because it filters blanks out again on the way in.
      ;;
    *)
      echo "settings.map: $name has an unknown disposition '$how'" >&2
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac
done < <(grep -vE '^\s*(#|$)' "$HERE/settings.map")

install -m 600 "$tmp" "$OUT"
echo "assembled $written settings into $OUT"
",
    "Error": ""
}

#!/bin/bash
# Replace what the platform box is running with a named build.
#
#   /opt/egma/deployment/deploy.sh <ref>
#
# The deploy workflow in the public repository invokes this over SSM, after
# syncing this whole directory fresh from S3. It is equally a script to run by
# hand on the box when nobody wants to drive a deployment through CI.
#
# ## The layout, and the rule behind it
#
#   /opt/egma/deployment/   this directory. Synced from S3 with --delete on
#                           every deploy, so nothing in it can drift — it IS
#                           the egma-cloud repository's deployment/ folder
#   /opt/egma/egma/         egma's own repository, checked out at the ref
#                           being deployed. Rebuilt whenever it is missing
#   /opt/egma/certs/        the Supabase root, fetched when missing
#   /opt/egma/.env          assembled fresh on every deploy, root-only
#
# Nothing under /opt/egma is authored on the box. Every file either arrives
# from a repository (via S3 or git) or is derived at deploy time. That rule is
# the fix for 2026-08-15, when hand-written files on this box drifted behind a
# rename in the code and took the persona's settings down silently.
set -euo pipefail

REF="${1:-latest}"
REGION="${AWS_REGION:-${AWS_DEFAULT_REGION:-us-east-1}}"
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
WORK="$(cd "$HERE/.." && pwd)"
CODE="$WORK/egma"

# ── egma's own files, at the commit the images were built from ───────────────
# The compose files and the images must come from one commit. Deploying an
# image built from one tree with compose files from another is how a setting
# goes missing without anything failing.
if [ -d "$CODE/.git" ]; then
  git -C "$CODE" fetch --tags --quiet origin
else
  git clone --quiet https://github.com/egma-ai/egma.git "$CODE"
fi
if git -C "$CODE" rev-parse --verify --quiet "$REF^{commit}" >/dev/null; then
  git -C "$CODE" checkout --quiet --detach "$REF"
  echo "egma files at $REF ($(git -C "$CODE" rev-parse --short HEAD))"
else
  git -C "$CODE" checkout --quiet --detach origin/main
  echo "no ref '$REF' in the repository; using origin/main for the compose files"
fi

# ── The Supabase root ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Fetched rather than committed: it is a published file, and its address is in
# the egma/db/supabase secret under ca_url. Without it the API dies at boot
# reporting a self-signed chain.
if [ ! -s "$WORK/certs/supabase-ca.crt" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$WORK/certs"
  curl -fsSL \
    "$(aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id egma/db/supabase \
        --region "$REGION" --query SecretString --output text \
      | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["ca_url"])')" \
    -o "$WORK/certs/supabase-ca.crt"
  echo "fetched the Supabase root certificate"
fi

# ── The settings ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Assembled fresh every time, so changing a secret and deploying is enough.
# assemble-env.sh refuses to write anything if settings.map does not answer
# every setting egma's compose files ask for — a gap stops the deployment here
# rather than reaching production.
bash "$HERE/assemble-env.sh" "$WORK/.env" "$CODE"

ACCOUNT="$(aws sts get-caller-identity --query Account --output text)"
REGISTRY="${EGMA_REGISTRY:-${ACCOUNT}.dkr.ecr.${REGION}.amazonaws.com}"

# The registry and tag join the assembled settings rather than being exported,
# so a `docker compose` run by hand afterwards sees exactly what the deployment
# saw rather than resolving to something else.
printf 'EGMA_REGISTRY=%s\nEGMA_IMAGE_TAG=%s\n' "$REGISTRY" "$REF" >> "$WORK/.env"

# One flag controls every platform telemetry path. The api and grader read it
# themselves. The collector is a Compose profile, so this deployment maps the
# same value to that profile. Anything but `on`, including an absent value,
# also removes a collector left running by an earlier enabled deployment.
PLATFORM_TELEMETRY="$(awk -F= '
  $1 == "EGMA_TELEMETRY" {
    value = substr($0, index($0, "=") + 1)
    gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", value)
    print tolower(value)
    exit
  }
' "$WORK/.env")"

COMPOSE_PROFILE_ARGS=()
if [ "$PLATFORM_TELEMETRY" = "on" ]; then
  COMPOSE_PROFILE_ARGS=(--profile platform-telemetry)
fi

# --project-directory anchors every relative path in the stack — ./certs, the
# env_file — to /opt/egma, whichever file names it.
compose() {
  docker compose \
    -f "$CODE/docker-compose.yml" \
    -f "$CODE/docker-compose.managed.yml" \
    -f "$HERE/local.yml" \
    --project-directory "$WORK" \
    --project-name egma "${COMPOSE_PROFILE_ARGS[@]}" "$@"
}

# Activate the collector profile only for this cleanup command. Stop and
# remove it before the rest of the deploy when the flag is off. A failed
# removal stops the deploy; it must not say telemetry is off while an old
# collector still sends data.
if [ "$PLATFORM_TELEMETRY" != "on" ]; then
  compose --profile platform-telemetry rm --stop --force otel-collector
  echo "platform telemetry: off"
fi

aws ecr get-login-password --region "$REGION" \
  | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin "$REGISTRY"

# `--no-build` matters: egma's compose file builds all three services from
# source, which is right for a self-hoster and wrong here. CI built these
# already, and this box holds a read-only pull credential on purpose.
compose pull
compose up -d --wait --wait-timeout 300 --no-build
compose ps
if [ "$PLATFORM_TELEMETRY" = "on" ]; then
  echo "platform telemetry: on"
fi

# ── The images nothing runs anymore ──────────────────────────────────────────
# Every deploy pulls three images tagged with their commit, and the box never
# needs an old set again: the registry keeps every tag, so a rollback re-pulls
# whatever it names. Left alone they only accumulate — 21 GB of them by
# 2026-08-17, 90% of everything docker held — and the only question about an
# unbounded pile is which day it fills the disk. Pruned only here, after the
# new containers are up and healthy, and prune
# never touches an image a container is using — so what is running, including
# everything a `deploy.sh <ref>` rollback would stop, is never the thing
# removed.
docker image prune -af
echo "pruned the images nothing runs"

#
# `deploy.sh` is the normal entry point. It enables the
# `platform-telemetry` profile only when EGMA_TELEMETRY is `on`.
#
# Everything egma is comes from the first two files, under review and under
# `deployment.test.ts`. This third file holds the two things that are ours
# alone, and nothing else. **If something can go in the public files, it goes
# there** — that is the rule that broke when the box ran a whole hand-written
# compose file and drifted a day behind a rename.

  # **The certificate, and the one line that makes it count.**
  #
  # Supabase signs its pooler with its own private CA — `*.pooler.supabase.com`
  # → `Supabase Intermediate 2021 CA` → `Supabase Root 2021 CA` — and that root
  # is in no public trust store. `pg` 8.22 verifies the chain where older
  # versions shrugged, so without this the API dies at boot reporting a
  # self-signed chain rather than a missing certificate.
  #
  # The alternative is `sslmode=no-verify`, and it is not an alternative. It
  # turns a verified connection into a merely encrypted one, and what that
  # protects is `EGMA_ENCRYPTION_KEY`'s work: the sealed **connection**
  # credentials of every customer. An encrypted connection to an attacker is
  # still a connection to an attacker.
  #
  # `deploy.sh` fetches the certificate before this file is ever read. Its
  # address is in the `egma/db/supabase` secret under `ca_url`.
  # **`image:` is the second thing this file is for.** egma's own compose file
  # builds all three services from source, which is right for a self-hoster and
  # wrong here: CI already built these, pushed them to ECR, and the box has a
  # read-only pull credential on purpose. Naming the image makes `pull` fetch
  # what CI made instead of the box compiling it again on a t3.large.
  #
  # `deploy.sh` appends EGMA_REGISTRY and EGMA_IMAGE_TAG to .env, so a run by
  # hand afterwards resolves to exactly what the deployment resolved to.
  api:
    image: ${EGMA_REGISTRY}/egma/api:${EGMA_IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
